newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Oversold position on SAfrica fwd book falls in Q1.
newsitem.headline: Oversold position on SAfrica fwd book falls in Q1.

text.p: The Reserve Bank's net oversold position on its forward book had fallen by one billion dollars by March 31 and was expected to fall further as confidence in the rand increased, Governor Chris Stals said on Tuesday.
"On December 31 1996, the net oversold position amounted to $22.2 billion, and on March 31 to $21.2 billion," Stals told Reuters on Tuesday.
"It is expected that the book will decline further as confidence will rise in the stability of the exchange rate of the rand," he added.

Last week, the Finance Department announced that due to profits being realised on the Reserve Bank's provision of forward cover during the first quarter of 1997, the deficit on the gold and foreign exchange contingency reserve acount amounted to 2.169 billion rand, down from a previous estimate of a 3.652 billion rand deficit.
Stals said that while the central bank was not prepared to comment on the current level of the exchange rate, it welcomed the more stable conditions over recent months.
After firming around twenty cents since the beginning of the year, the rand has traded at between 4.40 and 4.50 against the dollar since early February.
The dollar's recent gains against the yen and Deutschmark have also resulted in the rand improving on a trade-weighted basis.
